The test image shows a corn leaf with a large, elongated (cigar/canoe-shaped) tan to gray lesion several inches long with darker brown margins. There are also scattered small reddish-brown spots. This is a **leaf** disease.

Top candidates from the leaf class list: Northern_Leaf_Blight, Goss_S_Wilt, Stewart_S_Disease, Southern_Corn_Leaf_Blight, Anthracnose_Leaf_Spot_And_Top_Dieback, Gray_Leaf_Spot, Eyespot, Holcus_Spot.

Let me view one reference from each top candidate, starting with the most likely.
NLB reference shows cigar-shaped tan lesions, very similar to the test image. Let me check other candidates.
Goss's Wilt looks very different - extensive water-soaked lesions with wavy edges. Not a match. Let me check more candidates.
Stewart's shows linear bleached streaks along veins - different from the test image's discrete cigar-shaped lesion.
SCLB shows smaller, rectangular lesions confined by veins - very different from the test image's large cigar-shaped lesion.
Anthracnose shows smaller, darker lesions at leaf margins with dark brown/purple borders - different pattern from the test image.
Gray Leaf Spot shows narrow, rectangular lesions bounded by veins - very different from the large cigar-shaped lesion in the test image.
Eyespot shows many small circular spots with yellow halos - completely different pattern. Now let me use my last view to confirm NLB with another reference.

This second NLB reference shows severe infection with large tan lesions on multiple leaves, consistent with the disease pattern.

**Analysis summary:**
- The test image shows a large, cigar/canoe-shaped tan to gray lesion several inches long with darker brown margins on a corn leaf
- This is the classic Northern Leaf Blight presentation
- The NLB reference (Corn_Disease_127) showed nearly identical cigar-shaped tan lesions
- All other candidates were clearly different: Goss's Wilt (extensive water-soaked with freckles), Stewart's (linear streaks), SCLB (small rectangular), Anthracnose (small dark-margined), Gray Leaf Spot (narrow rectangular), Eyespot (small circular spots)
- The scattered small reddish spots on the test image are secondary and the dominant lesion is the diagnostic feature
